name: Learn a choreographed dance
blurb: One full routine, learned properly and performed. Choreography teaches counting, spatial memory and the difference between knowing the steps and actually performing them.
gear: A tutorial video that breaks it down by count
A mirror or a filming setup
steps: Pick a routine within reach — a well-known 60 to 90 second sequence with a good breakdown tutorial.
Learn it in 8-count chunks, mastering each before joining them.
Practise at half speed with the count spoken out loud, then to music.
Join chunks in overlapping pairs, because the transitions are where routines fall apart.
Film yourself and compare side by side with the original — arm angles and timing are always worse than they feel.
Perform it at full speed, full energy, for someone.
tips: Learning to the music too early hides mistakes. Get the counts clean first.
Performance energy is a separate skill from the steps. Practise it deliberately.
proof: You perform the full routine to music, from memory, at full speed, on camera.
